"Create a first-person shooter roguelite with RPG progression, set in a post-apocalyptic Russian city. Gritty, darkly humorous tone. Visual style: dirty realism, muted palette (gray, blue, dirty yellow), no cyberpunk. Inspired by Hotline Miami, Enter the Gungeon, Skul, Gunfire Reborn.

PLAYER: A tired guy in a hoodie and sneakers. Sprint, dodge roll, slide. FPS shooting, fast reload, kick (stuns and knocks back enemies). No melee weapons. Health 100, out-of-combat regen plus small heal per kill. Status effects on enemies: stun, burning, freezing, bleeding.

WEAPONS: All weapons are improvised from household junk (no real guns). Three classes: Strength (slow, powerful), Balance (versatile), Agility (fast, weak). Examples: paint roller (splashes elemental paint), construction stapler, angle grinder, extension cord with plug (electric shock), toaster (shoots red-hot bolts), blowtorch, kettle, gas canister. Starter weapon \"Leaky Pipe\": infinite ammo, low damage, cannot be upgraded. Rarity: Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary. Upgraded at the Blacksmith for scrap metal; each rank changes the visual model. Weapon upgrades reset on death to force experimentation. Some weapons start at Common, others start at Rare.

WORLD (beta route): Center, Industrial Zone, Residential District, Port. Each ends with a boss. After each boss, a room contains two NPCs: Blacksmith and Dispatcher.

KEYS: To unlock the next location, find a key in the current location and carry it to the end. If you die holding a key, it is lost and respawns elsewhere. Hand keys to the Dispatcher after the boss.

ECONOMY, THREE CURRENCIES:
1. Credits (in-run): from enemies. Spent on chests. Leftovers after a boss convert to max HP (1 credit = 0.5% HP, capped at +25% per stage).
2. Scrap Metal (in-run): only from dismantling unwanted weapons. Spent at the Blacksmith to upgrade your weapon. Lost on death.
3. Components (meta): from bosses, secret rooms, challenges. Persist between runs. Spent at the Dispatcher to permanently unlock new weapons, passive items, skins, enemy factions, and starting bonuses.

CHESTS, 4 color-coded tiers: Common (gray, mostly common loot), Rare (green, mostly rare loot), Epic (purple, mostly epic loot), Legendary (gold, guaranteed legendary plus 2 passive items). Chest prices scale with stage. Credit drops are capped per stage at the total cost of all chests plus a 10% bonus.

ENEMIES: Factions include Rusted (zombies), Stalkers (raiders), Mutants, Robots, Bandits, Deep Ones. Center has 3 types (melee, ranged, heavy). Later stages add flying, buffer, spawner, bomber. Elites appear from stage 3 with immunities and bonus loot.

BOSSES: Center tutorial mini-boss. Industrial Zone: \"Craneman\", a giant built from pipes and conveyors with a crane arm; phase 2 he magnetically pulls in scrap and gets aggressive; weak spots are hydraulics and exposed wires. Residential District: \"Mad Dog\", a fast mutant with floor traps. Port: \"Deep Leviathan\", 3 phases with a weak point and summoned waves.

NPCs:
- Blacksmith: bearded man in a leather apron at an anvil. Upgrades weapons for scrap metal, striking them with a hammer; sparks fly in the color of the new rarity and the model transforms.
- Dispatcher: old technician at a desk with city maps. Accepts keys to permanently unlock locations, gives hints on key locations, and sells permanent unlocks for Components.

CHALLENGES: Automatic achievements (kill 1000 enemies, beat a boss without damage, find secret rooms) that directly grant weapons, items, or skins without any currency.

PROTOTYPE SCOPE: one location (Center), 3 enemy types, 1 mini-boss, the starter Leaky Pipe, basic chests and credits, basic movement (sprint, dodge roll, kick). Exclude: melee weapons, cyberpunk, complex story, open world, multiplayer, persistent weapon upgrades between runs.

Build a playable vertical slice: movement, shooting, enemy AI, chest interaction, currency pickup, and a boss fight in the Center location. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.
- Prototype scope: Center location, three enemy types, mini-boss, Leaky Pipe starter weapon, credits/chests, movement, shooting, AI, and boss fight.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette; dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Player supports sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, and small heal per kill.
- Include chest interaction, enemy AI and currency pickups, plus a boss fight; support phone/tablet touch controls.
- User asked to build immediately, make reasonable assumptions, and note them briefly when finished; no clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based Three.js game with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI.
- Vertical slice uses three enemy archetypes (melee, ranged, heavy), three waves, and an original “Yard Foreman” boss with two phases.
- Used CDN import map for Three.js; no external 3D model assets added.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with game canvas, title/end screens, HUD, and touch control elements.
- Created `style.css` with gritty visual styling and responsive mobile HUD/touch controls.
- Created `game.js` implementing procedural 3D scene, player controls, weapons, enemies, drops, chests, waves, boss fight, and UI.

### Active
- Validate and fix the game implementation; verify it runs in browser and capture/inspect a screenshot.
- Check `game.js` as written: multiple full-file writes appear to have overwritten earlier code segments. Current file starts at `enemyProjectile()` and references undeclared globals/functions such as `THREE`, `scene`, `player`, `boss`, and `updateHud`; inspect current version and restore/merge full implementation as needed.

### Blocked
- Browser/game validation has not been done; the game may not run due to the suspected overwritten `game.js`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `game.js`; reconstruct a complete valid module if the earlier portions were overwritten.
2. Run syntax checks and launch the app in a browser; fix runtime errors and gameplay issues.
3. Test desktop and touch layouts/controls, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implementation, assumptions, and verification when finished.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, title/end screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, and touch control styles.
- `game.js`: Game logic; likely incomplete due to overwritten file content.

## Important Context
- The assistant created `game.js` in several successive full-file writes, and the final write replaced prior content; a later read showed only 72 lines, beginning with `enemyProjectile()` and lacking scene initialization.
- No tests, browser checks, screenshots, commits, or pushes have been performed.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, small health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.

- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, and a two-phase Yard Foreman boss; starter weapon is the Leaky Pipe.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, and a two-phase Yard Foreman boss; starter weapon is the Leaky Pipe.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with title/end screens, HUD, interaction prompt, and touch controls.
- Created `style.css` with gritty responsive styling and mobile controls.
- Implemented procedural courtyard scenery, player pipe attacks, enemy types and AI, waves, boss phases, kicks, rolls, health and regeneration, chests, currency drops, keyboard/mouse/touch controls, HUD, and render loop in `game.js`.
- Added touch-compatible chest button interaction and adjusted melee attack targeting/range.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` completed without errors.

### Active
- Validate runtime and gameplay in a browser; check console errors, controls, wave progression, and desktop/mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- Browser/gameplay verification and screenshots have not yet been completed.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:4173` in Playwright and inspect runtime and console.
2. Test starting, movement, attacking, chest interaction, wave progression, and touch controls; fix issues found.
3. Capture and inspect desktop and mobile screenshots, then summarize results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, procedural Three.js scene, input, and update/render loops.
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, start/end screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Visual design and responsive/touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push has been done.
- A local Python HTTP server was started on port `4173`; browser validation and screenshot capture remain pending.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element

  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page

  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, and a two-phase Yard Foreman boss; starter weapon is the Leaky Pipe.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, styling, procedural courtyard, combat, enemy AI, three waves and boss phases, pickups, chests, HUD, and keyboard/mouse/touch controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added touch-compatible chest interaction and adjusted melee attack targeting/range.
- Passed `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Installed Chromium and opened `http://localhost:4173`; confirmed the start screen works, starting the game reveals the HUD, and the initial wave spawns four hostiles.

### Active
- Validate gameplay, controls, wave progression, and desktop/mobile layouts in a browser; inspect screenshots and console.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, a two-phase Yard Foreman boss, and the Leaky Pipe starter weapon.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, styling, procedural courtyard, combat, enemy AI, three waves and boss phases, pickups, chests, HUD, and keyboard/mouse/touch controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added touch-compatible chest interaction and adjusted melee attack targeting/range.
- Passed `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Confirmed in Chromium that the start screen works and starting the game shows the HUD, 4 hostiles, and 100 health.
- Captured and inspected desktop and 390×844 mobile screenshots; the screenshots show game visuals, but mobile layout measurement returned suspiciously collapsed controls despite touch UI reporting `display: block`.

### Active
- Validate gameplay, controls, wave progression, and desktop/mobile layouts in a browser; diagnose the discrepant mobile layout measurements.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect mobile screenshot and stylesheet positioning; resolve the measured collapsed touch controls if they reflect a real layout issue.
2. Test movement, attack, chest interaction, and wave progression in Playwright.
3. Verify mobile touch inputs and desktop/mobile layouts; check browser console for runtime issues.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, a two-phase Yard Foreman boss, and the Leaky Pipe starter weapon.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, styling, procedural courtyard, combat, enemy AI, three waves and boss phases, pickups, chests, HUD, and keyboard/mouse/touch controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed malformed CSS in `.screen`’s gradient and restored the `.touch-ui{display:none}` rule.
- Verified at 390×844 that mobile action controls have visible, nonzero bounding boxes.
- Tested starting and moving: health stayed at 100 during sampled initial play.
- Verified chest prompt appears and pressing `E` opens the chest, awarding 31 credits in a sample run; no page errors observed in sampled tests.

### Active
- Validate firing, kick/roll, currency pickups, enemy kills, wave progression, and boss phases in a browser.
- Exercise mobile touch movement, aiming, and actions; inspect desktop/mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing combat actions, enemy kills, currency drops, wave transitions, and boss phases.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, a two-phase Yard Foreman boss, and the Leaky Pipe starter weapon.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, styling, procedural courtyard, combat, enemy AI, three waves and boss phases, pickups, chests, HUD, and keyboard/mouse/touch controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed malformed CSS in `.screen`’s gradient and restored the `.touch-ui{display:none}` rule.
- Verified at 390×844 that mobile action controls have visible, nonzero bounding boxes.
- Verified chest prompt appears and pressing `E` opens it, awarding 31 credits in a sample run; no page errors observed in that test.
- Reset transient gameplay and touch state on restart in `startGame()`; also reset boss HUD state.

### Active
- Validate firing, kick/roll, currency pickups, enemy kills, wave progression, and boss phases in a browser.
- Exercise mobile touch movement, aiming, and actions; inspect desktop/mobile layouts.
- Investigate combat testing: desktop pointer-locked fire test did not reduce the initial enemy count; touch simulation was inconclusive and sometimes ended in death without confirmed hits.

### Blocked
- Browser touch/combat tests have been unreliable due to synthetic pointer-event and pointer-capture behavior; no confirmed full combat or boss progression test yet.

## Next Move
1. Reload the page after the `startGame()` reset changes and check browser console for runtime errors.
2. Validate combat and progression using real browser input or reliable test instrumentation; confirm enemy kills, currency pickup, waves, and boss phases.
3. Re-test mobile movement, aiming, and action controls, then check responsive layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, procedural Three.js scene, input, and update/render loops.
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, start/end screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, and touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status`; no commit or push has been done.
- Local server is running on port `4173`; Chromium and `playwright-cli` are available.
- A prior browser test showed health remained at 100 during sampled initial play; a touch test also reduced enemies from 4 to 3, but did not establish reliable control behavior.

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, a two-phase Yard Foreman boss, and the Leaky Pipe starter weapon.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, styling, procedural courtyard, combat, enemy AI, waves and boss phases, pickups, chests, HUD, and keyboard/mouse/touch controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed malformed CSS gradient and restored `.touch-ui{display:none}`; verified mobile action controls have visible, nonzero bounds.
- Verified chest interaction awards credits; no errors were observed in that test.
- Reset transient gameplay/touch state and boss HUD state in `startGame()`.
- `node --check game.js` passed; latest browser console check reported no errors or warnings.

### Active
- Validate firing, kick/roll, currency pickups, enemy kills, wave progression, and boss phases.
- Verify mobile movement, aiming, and action controls, and inspect desktop/mobile layouts.
- Diagnose inconsistent browser input tests: movement and pointer lock were observed, but firing has not been confirmed to damage enemies.

### Blocked
- Combat/progression verification remains unreliable: sampled firing left all four initial hostiles alive, while a later run ended in death without confirmed hits.

## Next Move
1. Reload and verify the current `startGame()` reset changes and desktop input behavior.
2. Find a reliable way to validate aiming/fire damage, then confirm kills, drops, wave changes, and both boss phases.
3. Re-test touch controls and responsive layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, game logic, combat, progression, and input.
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, and touch controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git status. No commit or push has been done.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:4173/`; Chromium and `playwright-cli` are available.
- Browser tests have produced inconsistent results; do not treat combat or full progression as verified.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, a two-phase Yard Foreman boss, and the Leaky Pipe starter weapon.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, styling, procedural courtyard, combat, enemy AI, waves and boss phases, pickups, chests, HUD, and keyboard/mouse/touch controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed malformed CSS gradient and restored `.touch-ui{display:none}`; verified mobile action controls have visible, nonzero bounds during gameplay.
- Verified chest interaction awards credits; no errors were observed in that test.
- Reset transient gameplay/touch state and boss HUD state in `startGame()`.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser console check reported no errors or warnings.
- Confirmed desktop firing can damage and kill an enemy when pointer lock is active and the aim is turned toward a target.

### Active
- Validate currency pickup collection, wave progression, and both boss phases.
- Verify mobile movement, aiming, firing, and action controls; prior mobile test clicks did not confirm combat damage.
- Inspect desktop/mobile layouts and continue playability testing.

### Blocked
- Full combat/progression verification remains incomplete; no reliable validation yet for drops, later waves, or boss phases.

## Next Move
1. Continue desktop playtesting: confirm kill drops/credit pickup, wave 2 and wave 3, and both Foreman phases.
2. Test touch inputs using touch/pointer events rather than mouse-only gestures; verify movement, aiming, firing, kick, and roll.
3. Recheck responsive layouts and browser console after tests.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, game logic, combat, progression, and input.
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, and touch controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git status. No commit or push has been done.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:4173/`; Chromium and `playwright-cli` are available.
- Desktop firing test requires pointer lock, then a mouse movement toward a target; firing while aimed reduced enemy HP and eventually removed one hostile.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, a two-phase Yard Foreman boss, and the Leaky Pipe starter weapon.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, styling, procedural courtyard, combat, enemy AI, waves and boss phases, pickups, chests, HUD, and keyboard/mouse/touch controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed malformed CSS gradient and restored `.touch-ui{display:none}`; verified mobile action controls have visible, nonzero bounds during gameplay.
- Verified chest interaction awards credits; no errors were observed in that test.
- Reset transient gameplay/touch state and boss HUD state in `startGame()`.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser console check reported no errors or warnings.
- Confirmed desktop firing can damage and kill an enemy when pointer lock is active and the aim is turned toward a target.
- Verified simulated touch-pointer events move and reset both virtual sticks; firing killed an enemy and advanced play from wave 1 to wave 2, then to the final shift.

### Active
- Validate currency pickup collection, wave progression through wave 2, and both boss phases.
- Verify mobile kick, roll, sprint, and reliable touch combat/progression.
- Inspect desktop/mobile layouts and recheck browser console after tests.

### Blocked
- Full combat/progression verification remains incomplete; the latest mobile test reached the final shift but did not clear it or verify either boss phase.
- Currency pickup collection has not been confirmed.

## Next Move
1. Continue combat testing through the final shift; confirm the Yard Foreman’s phase transition and defeat.
2. Confirm kill-drop currency pickup collection and test mobile kick, roll, and sprint.
3. Recheck responsive layouts and browser console after testing.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, game logic, combat, progression, and input.
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, and touch controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git status. No commit or push has been done.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:4173/`; Chromium and `playwright-cli` are available.
- Desktop firing test requires pointer lock, then a mouse movement toward a target; firing while aimed reduced enemy HP and eventually removed a hostile.
- Mobile progression tests used synthetic pointer events; they reached `FINAL SHIFT` with four hostiles remaining, but did not establish the boss phase state.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 3D FPS roguelite vertical slice set in a gritty post-apocalyptic Russian city.

## Requirements
- Muted dirty-realism palette and dark humor; no cyberpunk or real guns/melee weapons.
- Include sprint, dodge roll, kick, out-of-combat health regeneration, health restored per kill, chest interaction, enemies, currency pickups, and a boss fight.
- Support keyboard/mouse and phone/tablet touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural low-poly courtyard scenery and UI; no external 3D models.
- Build the Center courtyard with three enemy types, three waves, a two-phase Yard Foreman boss, and the Leaky Pipe starter weapon.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, styling, procedural courtyard, combat, enemy AI, waves and boss phases, pickups, chests, HUD, and keyboard/mouse/touch controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed malformed CSS gradient and restored mobile touch control visibility; verified mobile action controls have visible, nonzero bounds during play.
- Verified chest interaction awards credits; desktop firing can damage and kill enemies with pointer lock and aiming; synthetic touch-stick input moves and resets both sticks, and touch firing can kill enemies and advance waves.
- Reset transient gameplay/touch state and boss HUD state in `startGame()`.
- Added coarse-pointer tablet touch controls for viewports wider than 700px; moved tablet HUD controls higher and hid the desktop controls hint to avoid overlap.
- Checked touch-control bounds at 390×844 mobile and 768×1024 tablet; all action buttons fit on-screen. Desktop canvas sizing checked at 1440×900.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed; browser console showed no errors or warnings.

### Active
- Validate currency pickup collection and complete the three-wave progression, including both boss phases and defeat.
- Verify mobile kick, roll, sprint, and reliable touch combat/progression under gameplay conditions.

### Blocked
- Full combat/progression verification remains incomplete: prior synthetic mobile combat reached `FINAL SHIFT` with hostiles remaining but did not confirm the boss phase transition or defeat.
- Currency pickup collection has not been confirmed.

## Next Move
1. Continue combat testing through the final shift; confirm the Yard Foreman’s phase transition and defeat.
2. Confirm kill-drop currency pickup collection and test mobile kick, roll, and sprint.
3. Recheck responsive layouts and browser console after tests.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, combat, progression, and input.
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, screens, and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, and touch controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files remain untracked in git status. No commit or push has been done.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:4173/`; Chromium and `playwright-cli` are available.
- Desktop firing requires pointer lock, then aiming toward a target; firing while aimed reduced enemy HP and eventually removed a hostile.
- Touch action buttons were verified to have nonzero visible bounds on mobile and tablet. A prior extended synthetic combat attempt ended with player health at 0 before clearing wave 1, so it did not validate full touch progression.
